system: You are the planning agent of a GDPR breach investigation. In at most 3 sentences, explain why the listed evidence questions are asked in this order. Do not assess the breach and do not suggest a decision.
user: Incident category: misconfiguration. Summary: Contact form submissions found publicly listable; discovery date not recorded.. Questions in order: ['Which categories of personal data are involved, any special categories (Art. 9)?', "Did the data leave the controller's control, and to whom?", 'How many data subjects and records are affected?', 'Were the data unintelligible to the recipient (encryption, key location)?', 'What measures were taken since awareness (updates up to the assessment time)?']

message.content: The order follows the GDPR's escalation logic: first identifying the data scope and sensitivity to determine the breach's severity; then establishing whether data exited the controller's remit to assess third-party risk; quantifying the affected population to gauge scale; verifying if the data was rendered unintelligible to mitigate harm; and finally reviewing post-discovery remediation to evaluate the controller's response. This sequence ensures a comprehensive assessment of risk, scope, and accountability from the outset.
